lessons.title: A story in three still pictures
lessons.outcome: Use freeze-frame/role-play to tell a story.
lessons.goal: I can use still poses to tell a short story.
success: I can show first, next and last.
I can choose a pose or direct one.
I can keep one real choice in my arts log.
words: A still pose that shows one part of a story.
A made-up person in a story.
A sign to start or stop.
Things that happen in an order.

artist_cards.description: A helper looks at an empty shelf. The helper pauses with open hands. A friend points to a box. They both look in the box. They smile when the prop is found.
artist_cards.prompt: How does a still pose help us follow the story?
artist_cards.model_answer: The empty hands and look towards the shelf show a missing prop. The pause gives the viewer time to notice it.

artist_cards.description: Two makers hold an imaginary large sheet. They stop when it will not fit. One points to a fold. They fold the sheet in mime, then carry it together with space between them.
artist_cards.prompt: How does the second action show a new plan?
artist_cards.model_answer: They fold the sheet in mime so it fits. The action after the pause makes the change clear. Nobody needs a real prop or contact.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Choose act, direct or watch first.
Point, speak, sign or pass.
Use made-up roles today.
stages.say: Choose how to join in. We will tell a made-up story. You can sit, direct me or try a pose. Our open hand means stop.
stages.good: Every pupil has a participation choice and knows the stop cue.
stages.fallback: Offer two choices: direct me or use one hand. A pupil may watch first.
stages.answer: Acting, directing and a seated pose are all valid. Watching first is a preparation choice; record a later contribution accurately.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Watch a still pose: look at an empty shelf.
What might be lost?
Watch a smile and a point. What may come next?
stages.say: My empty hands and look show a missing prop. My point shows an idea. Can we tell which comes first? These are invented signs, not rules about feelings.
stages.good: Pupils notice a concrete feature and link it to a story part.
stages.fallback: Show the two poses seated. Ask the pupil to point to first.
stages.answer: Looking at the empty shelf can begin the story. A point can show a plan. Accept another clear order if the pupil explains it.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch first, next and last.
First: the prop is lost.
Next: the helper looks in a box.
Last: the prop is found.
stages.say: I show three still pictures. First I look at the empty shelf. Next I point into a box. Last I hold an imaginary prop and smile. I hold each pose for two seconds and relax. I try the last pose facing away, then facing you. Facing you makes my choice easier to see.
stages.good: Adult models a complete three-part invented story, a comfortable freeze and one deliberate improvement.
stages.fallback: Mime with hands on a table or describe each part while pointing to three spaces.
stages.answer: The problem is a missing prop. Looking in a box is the action. Finding it is the ending. Ask: Which pose shows the end? Check before moving on.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Choose a helper and a friend.
Pick first, next and last.
Try three still poses with space.
Which pose helps us see the end?
stages.say: Let us use the lost prop story. You choose where I look first. A partner or adult can be the friend. We move only at walking pace and do not touch. After each cue, relax. If the ending is unclear, change one hand or face direction.
stages.good: Each pupil chooses a story detail. The group rehearses a shared cue and improves one pose.
stages.fallback: One pupil directs the adult through three seated poses. Ask the next pupil to choose a different final pose.
stages.answer: A clear end might show the found prop. If pupils cannot order the parts, return to two parts: lost, found; then add the search. This is the hinge decision.

stages.name: Create
pupil: In your book, mark first, next and last.
Use our story or make a safe new one.
Try three poses. Keep space.
Change one pose to help the viewer.
Tell an adult what you chose.
stages.say: Work in a pair, or in a small group with an adult. Choose the lost prop or a folded sheet that now fits. Give each person a pose or a directing job. Take turns choosing. Rehearse, ask one viewer what they saw, then change one pose. I will note your real choice.
stages.good: Each pupil makes or directs an intentional pose. The sequence has a beginning, action and ending, with one tested change.
stages.fallback: Use three small sketches or table-top hand poses. Adult acts only the pupil directions. A pupil may show just two parts first, then choose a third.
stages.answer: Example only: empty hands, point in box, hold found prop. A new safe invented sequence is equally valid. Record what the pupil actually did, not the example.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Choose one pose to show.
You may show just the adult.
Say: I notice ___.
Relax and clear your space.
stages.say: Choose a partner or a private adult audience. The viewer says what they saw, then asks the maker to confirm. Keep feedback about the story. In the last two minutes, return chairs safely and store the plan.
stages.good: Pupil shares a choice with an agreed audience and hears one specific observation.
stages.fallback: Adult describes the directed pose and asks the pupil to confirm the intended part.
stages.answer: Useful feedback: I saw you point in the box. That helped me see the search. Avoid guessing private feelings.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: I showed ___.
I chose ___ because ___.
Next time I will ___.
stages.say: Show your plan or describe your real pose. I can write your words and read them back. You can change them. We will use this sequence again tomorrow, or make a fresh one if needed.
stages.good: Dated entry records the pupil role, chosen pose, reason and actual support.
stages.fallback: Offer first, next or last as choices. Scribe only the confirmed response.
stages.answer: Example only: I pointed in the box to show a search. Next time I will face the viewer.

Supported: Pick lost prop or folded sheet.
Choose first, next and last with an adult.
Make a seated pose or direct the adult.
Point to one pose to keep in your log.
Independent: Plan first, next and last in your book.
Rehearse three poses with a partner.
Ask what the viewer can see.
Change one pose and log your reason.
Aspire: Try two ways to show the ending.
Choose the clearer one. Say why.
Give your partner a calm start cue.

log: My role was act / direct / seated gesture.
misconceptions: A freeze-frame means hold still for a long time
Hold a comfortable pose for two seconds, then relax. Seated or hand poses count.
A good story needs real events from my life
Use an invented prop or folded sheet story. No personal disclosure is needed.
The loudest actor tells the clearest story
A clear pose, space and order can tell the story in silence.
kit: For three to four pupils: books or arts logs and pencils.
Clear a safe acting area. Keep chairs available for seated work.
No props, costumes, devices or sound equipment are needed.
Retain the three-part plans and dated observations for the next lesson.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Look at an empty shelf with empty hands. Say: First, the prop is lost.
15 to 30 seconds
Point into an imaginary box. Say: Next, I search.
30 to 45 seconds
Hold an imaginary prop. Say: Last, I find it.
45 to 60 seconds
Turn the last pose towards the viewer. Say: I changed this so you can see the end.
models: Teacher model only: I showed empty hands, a search and a found prop. I faced the viewer so the ending was clear.

staff_guidance.plain_language: A pause, a request for help or a new plan can show resilience. Pupils do not need to act out real distress or tell a personal story.
staff_guidance.scope: Both pathways work at Explore. Retain actual participation, exploration, creation and sharing evidence for the award. These lessons do not certify completion. Optional next level work in GROW is additional.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: Model a tiny invented action slowly. A clear choice matters more than expert acting. A pupil may direct an adult, use a seated gesture or describe the action.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Agree an open-hand stop signal and a quiet return cue. Keep voices at talking level. Allow pass, private sharing and a calm pause. Do not use sudden noises, personal stories or forced eye contact.
staff_guidance.safety: Clear bags and chairs from the acting area. Mark personal space by agreement; no touch, lifting, chasing, falls, climbing, weapons or thrown objects. Mime props. A still pose may be seated and lasts only a comfortable few seconds.
prompt_ladder: Point to the place or instruction.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Show one story part at a time. Rehearse first, next and last. Use two choices and fade prompts.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Offer point, sign, speech, drawing or a pupil-directed adult. Give thinking time. Repeat the pupil choice for confirmation.
adaptations.semh: Use invented roles. Agree audience and opt-out before rehearsal. Give each pupil a real choice without a public performance demand.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Offer seated, silent or directing roles. Keep walking pace and safe personal space. Stop if a pose is uncomfortable.
adaptations.eal: Plan in any language. Show freeze, move and share with gestures. Accept labels, drawings or an oral response before a full sentence.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Performers, directors and stage teams listen to cues, test ideas and explain their choices.

cold_call.middle: What helps us see the change?
cold_call.higher: Which choice makes the story clearer, and why?

ta_focus.I do: Point to the model choice. Ask the pupil to identify a detail before explaining it.
ta_focus.We do: Give one short cue. Return the next decision to the pupil.
ta_focus.Independent: Record the help actually used. Accept a directed adult or seated contribution as real participation.

lessons.evidence: Keep the actual story plan, dated observation and pupil-confirmed arts-log words. Record the contribution and help used. A photograph or recording is optional and follows local consent procedures. Model examples are never entered as pupil evidence.
lessons.artist_use_note: Both performance cards are invented original classroom examples. They are not a claim of an artist encounter or of pupil evidence. No published story, lyrics or dialogue is reproduced.
lessons.cover: Read each stage aloud and model the lost prop sequence in three still poses. Use no props. Let pupils act seated or direct an adult. Plan, rehearse, change one pose and keep the pupil-confirmed arts-log entry. Share only with an agreed audience. The seven stage times total 40 minutes.

lessons.title: A story with a short role-play
lessons.outcome: Use freeze-frame/role-play to tell a story.
lessons.goal: I can add a short action or line to our story.
success: I can keep first, next and last clear.
I can add one action or short line.
I can share and log a real choice.
words: Act as a made-up person in a story.
Show an action without a real object.

artist_cards.description: A helper looks at an empty shelf. The helper pauses with open hands. A friend points to a box. They both look in the box. They smile when the prop is found.
artist_cards.prompt: How does a still pose help us follow the story?
artist_cards.model_answer: The empty hands and look towards the shelf show a missing prop. The pause gives the viewer time to notice it.

artist_cards.description: Two makers hold an imaginary large sheet. They stop when it will not fit. One points to a fold. They fold the sheet in mime, then carry it together with space between them.
artist_cards.prompt: How does the second action show a new plan?
artist_cards.model_answer: They fold the sheet in mime so it fits. The action after the pause makes the change clear. Nobody needs a real prop or contact.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Choose act, direct or sit.
Find your story plan if it is here.
A fresh plan is fine.
stages.say: We can build on yesterday or make a fresh lost prop story. Missing work is not a problem to hide. We record what we do today. Choose how to join in and check the open-hand stop cue.
stages.good: Every pupil has access to a usable story, including absent pupils.
stages.fallback: Adult recalls the lost prop model in three hand poses. Pupil chooses a beginning or end.
stages.answer: A recovered plan and a fresh plan are both valid. Do not backdate a new plan.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Show or direct one still pose.
Is it first, next or last?
What could the role say?
stages.say: I show the empty shelf. A helper might say: Where is the prop? Or the helper can point in silence. Which helps our story?
stages.good: Pupil recalls a pose and selects a possible short line or action.
stages.fallback: Offer two lines: Where is it? or Here it is! Ask which fits this pose.
stages.answer: Where is it? fits the problem; Here it is! fits the ending. Silent mime can communicate either.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch a pose, a line and a move.
I say: Where is the prop?
I look in the box.
I say: Here it is! Then I freeze.
stages.say: I keep the same order. I start in my empty-hands pose, say one short line at talking level, mime looking in the box and end in my found-prop pose. I try rushing, then add a pause. The pause gives the viewer time. I do not need to shout.
stages.good: Adult models brief role-play bounded by two poses and tests a pause.
stages.fallback: Do the full sequence seated with hand mime and a whispered or adult-spoken line.
stages.answer: The first line shows the problem. The move shows the search. The final line and pose show the result. Ask: Which bit shows the search?

stages.name: We do
pupil: Pick one line or silent action.
Try it between two poses.
Give a calm cue.
Ask: Could you follow the story?
stages.say: You choose the line or mime. I will wait for the cue. Let us try a short pause before the end. The viewer says first and last. If the order is unclear, return to three still pictures and add only one move.
stages.good: Each pupil contributes a line, action or directing decision. The group checks whether a viewer follows the order.
stages.fallback: Adult performs the pupil choices. Pupil points when the adult should pause.
stages.answer: A viewer naming lost then found shows a clear order. If not, keep the freezes and add one action only. This is the hinge decision.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Use your plan or make a fresh one.
Add one move or short line.
Keep voices calm and leave space.
Try it, ask for one note, then try again.
Log what you chose.
stages.say: In a pair or adult-supported group, agree one line or move per role. A directing job counts when it includes a real choice. Rehearse for a short agreed audience. Ask: Which part was clear? Change a pause, facing or cue. A silent version is complete.
stages.good: The role-play retains a clear three-part story, an intentional addition and one revision informed by feedback.
stages.fallback: Make a seated hand drama. Adult voices the pupil-selected line. Pupil may direct a start and a pause without speaking.
stages.answer: Example only: Where is the prop? Search mime. Here it is! A quiet original line or silent action is equally valid.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Share a small part or the whole story.
Choose your audience.
Say: I saw ___ in your story.
Put plans away with care.
stages.say: Choose a peer, a small group or the adult. Listen to one story detail. Ask the maker if the meaning was understood. In the last two minutes, reset chairs and store the plan beside the log.
stages.good: Pupil has an agreed sharing moment and receives a specific, respectful observation.
stages.fallback: Adult repeats the chosen action, then reads the viewer note for confirmation.
stages.answer: A useful note is: Your pause helped me see the ending. Comment on a choice, not on acting confidence or personal traits.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: I added ___.
Our viewer noticed ___.
Next time I will ___.
stages.say: Keep your own words about the action or line you chose. I will date the record today and note the help used. If you did not share today, we write that honestly and plan a later private share.
stages.good: Record distinguishes performance, creation and sharing actually completed, with an honest next step.
stages.fallback: Offer point, short phrase or dictated sentence. Read it back.
stages.answer: Example only: I added a pause. The viewer saw the prop was found. Next time I will face front.

Supported: Choose one short line or a silent move.
Act seated or direct an adult.
Keep one choice in your arts log.
Independent: Use or make a three-part plan.
Add a line, mime or pause.
Rehearse and ask for one clear note.
Try a change and log what helped.
Aspire: Keep the same core story task.
Try a silent version and a spoken one.
Choose which tells the story best.
Explain the effect of your pause or cue.

log: Today I used a previous plan / a fresh plan.
misconceptions: Role-play needs lots of words
One short line or a silent action can tell the story.
A missing old plan means no lesson today
Make a fresh plan and date it today.
Feedback means telling someone they are good or bad
Notice a clear action, line, pose or pause and say how it helps the story.
kit: For three to four pupils: books or arts logs and pencils.
Clear a safe acting area. Keep chairs available for seated work.
No props, costumes, devices or sound equipment are needed.
Retain the three-part plans and dated observations for the next lesson.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show empty hands. Say: Where is the prop?
15 to 30 seconds
Mime looking in a box. Keep the body in personal space.
30 to 45 seconds
Pause, show an imaginary prop and say: Here it is!
45 to 60 seconds
Repeat the last part facing the viewer. Say: I chose a pause so the end was clear.
models: Teacher model only: I added a search mime and a pause before Here it is! I kept the order so the viewer could follow it.

lessons.title: Find the story in our arts logs
lessons.outcome: Share Explore/Bronze portfolio evidence so far.
lessons.goal: I can select real arts evidence and explain one choice.
success: I can find or make a genuine dated entry.
I can explain what I did and the help I used.
I can choose evidence and a safe audience to share it.
words: Real work or a record of what you actually did.
A collection of your arts work and records.
The part you chose or did.
Something that still needs a real record.

artist_cards.description: A helper looks at an empty shelf. The helper pauses with open hands. A friend points to a box. They both look in the box. They smile when the prop is found.
artist_cards.prompt: How does a still pose help us follow the story?
artist_cards.model_answer: The empty hands and look towards the shelf show a missing prop. The pause gives the viewer time to notice it.

artist_cards.description: Two makers hold an imaginary large sheet. They stop when it will not fit. One points to a fold. They fold the sheet in mime, then carry it together with space between them.
artist_cards.prompt: How does the second action show a new plan?
artist_cards.model_answer: They fold the sheet in mime so it fits. The action after the pause makes the change clear. Nobody needs a real prop or contact.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Choose a private or small audience.
Gather the arts logs that are here.
If yours is missing, use today's fresh task.
stages.say: Today we review real evidence before sharing it. A missing log is a gap to plan for, not a reason to invent an entry. You choose the audience. No one has to explain a personal experience.
stages.good: Pupils have an agreed audience option and access to old logs or a fresh route.
stages.fallback: Adult offers a clean page and a short invented drama task.
stages.answer: Work present today can be reviewed. Work that cannot be found is recorded as unavailable, not completed.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Compare: a blank log and a real dated entry.
Which shows what happened?
What extra detail would help?
stages.say: A title alone does not show what the maker did. A dated note such as I directed a two-pose story tells us more. We can add a confirmed explanation today without changing the old date.
stages.good: Pupil distinguishes a claim from evidence and identifies one helpful detail.
stages.fallback: Read two short oral examples and offer shows my choice / does not show it yet.
stages.answer: A real record with a date, contribution and pupil explanation is stronger than a blank page or model answer. A new explanation uses today's date.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch an adult sort model evidence.
Find: what, when, my part, my choice.
Mark clear, needs a note or missing.
Keep model evidence separate from your own.
stages.say: This invented adult sample has a drama plan and a dated note. I can tell who chose the pause and why. I mark it clear. This blank page needs evidence. This claim of a show has no record; I mark missing. These samples cannot become your evidence. I read the lost prop and new plan cards as invented performance examples only.
stages.good: Adult models an honest audit, explains source/date and keeps examples separate.
stages.fallback: Use three spoken labels with one adult sample at a time.
stages.answer: Clear means enough detail to understand a real contribution; needs a note means a real item exists but lacks explanation; missing means no item is available. Check with one item before independent sorting.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Try one record together with permission.
Ask: What did the maker do?
Ask: What choice is shown?
Choose one clear item or one honest gap.
stages.say: We can use an adult sample if no pupil wants to share. Read the record, ask the maker for permission and check its meaning. We do not guess that everyone attended. If it needs a note, the maker gives words we can confirm.
stages.good: Group applies the audit questions without inventing attendance, intentions or work.
stages.fallback: Use only the fictional adult sample. Pupil chooses the audit category and a useful question.
stages.answer: If the contribution is unclear, ask the maker once. If still unclear, mark needs a note. If no real record exists, use today's fresh task rather than recreate an old claim.

stages.name: Create
pupil: In your arts log, select up to three real items.
For each, find a date and your part.
Choose one item you could explain.
If no work is here, make a tiny drama now.
Plan one real gap to fill later.
stages.say: Use your existing arts log if available. Keep original dates and add new notes with today's date. Select rather than decorate. For a fresh route, make or direct a two-pose story: a folded sheet will not fit; a new fold makes it fit. Try a pause and choose the clearer version. I witness the actual contribution. Then plan a share for Wednesday.
stages.good: Each pupil selects genuine evidence or makes a witnessed fresh drama entry, confirms a contribution and identifies a feasible next step.
stages.fallback: Adult reads available records one at a time. Pupil points to one real choice. If none is available, direct the adult's two poses and confirm a dated observation.
stages.answer: Fresh example only: I directed the second pose and chose a pause to show the plan changed. Do not label it as a past lesson or live arts encounter.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Explain one selected item to your chosen viewer.
Say: My part was ___.
Viewer asks: What helped your idea?
Store the work for Wednesday.
stages.say: Share a small real detail privately or with a peer. The viewer asks a question, not a judgement. Confirm what was understood. Save the selected item and the audit note; use the last two minutes to reset the space.
stages.good: Pupil explains an actual contribution and confirms the viewer's reading.
stages.fallback: Adult reads the pupil-confirmed note aloud and records whether sharing occurred.
stages.answer: An explanation can be spoken, signed, sketched or scribed. Record a private share accurately; if declined, keep sharing as a future step.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: I selected or made ___.
This shows I ___.
My next step before sharing is ___.
stages.say: Keep the item reference, actual date, your words and the help used. A gap can stay open. Our record shows what happened, rather than claiming the award is finished.
stages.good: Evidence index separates available items, missing items and today's new work.
stages.fallback: Offer one item code and one short confirmed phrase.
stages.answer: Example only: Item one is my three-part plan. It shows I chose the ending. My next step is to explain why I chose it.

Supported: Review one real item with an adult.
Point to your part or explain it aloud.
If no item is here, direct a two-pose drama.
Keep a dated note and choose a viewer.
Independent: Audit up to three available items.
Record each date, your part and one choice.
Select an item and one honest gap.
Plan a short share with an agreed audience.
Aspire: Compare two items for what they show.
Explain which best shows a choice and why.
Set one precise evidence or skill goal.

log: Original date if known: ___. Today's note date: ___.
My agreed audience and next step: ___.
misconceptions: A finished-looking page proves participation
Check a real contribution, date and pupil-confirmed explanation. Decoration alone is not evidence.
Everyone must have the same past work
Do not assume attendance. Audit what exists and offer today's fresh witnessed task.
We should fill a gap with the teacher model
A model is only an example. Keep the gap open or collect new actual work with today's date.
Sharing the portfolio means the award is complete
This is a review of evidence so far. Further opportunities and an authorised review may still be needed.
kit: For up to five pupils: available arts logs, books and pencils.
Access only each pupil's permitted records. Cover identifying details when sharing.
Adult model audit page clearly labelled Teacher model only.
No recording device, costume, prop or internet is required.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Point to the dated adult model drama plan. Name the actual contribution it describes.
15 to 30 seconds
Read a reason for the pause. Mark the model clear.
30 to 45 seconds
Show a blank sample. Mark missing rather than inventing an entry.
45 to 60 seconds
Mime the fresh two-pose fold story and date the new witnessed record today.
models: Teacher model only: This dated plan shows I directed the ending. The note explains my pause. A blank page is still a gap, so I will make a new witnessed trial today.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Compare two real items. Explain which gives clearer evidence of your choice and why. Identify one skill goal and plan how you will check it.
stretch.evidence: Keep item references, your own comparison, the reason and a specific future check. Date new notes today.
stretch.why_optional: This adds reflection that may support a later level review. It is not needed for this lesson's Explore success criteria and does not certify completion of the award.
stretch.good: Pupil distinguishes actual contribution from a claim and gives a reasoned comparison based on available evidence.
stretch.fallback: Compare one real item with an honestly missing record. Keep the gap and set a new evidence opportunity; do not invent the absent item.

lessons.cover: Gather available arts logs. Model clear, needs a note and missing using an adult sample. Pupils audit up to three real items, select one and plan a safe share. If work is unavailable, use the folded-sheet two-pose drama and make a witnessed record dated today. Use the seven stage times and do not assume prior attendance.

lessons.title: Share a real arts choice
lessons.outcome: Share Explore/Bronze portfolio evidence so far.
lessons.goal: I can share genuine arts evidence and use one useful response.
success: I can explain my contribution and a choice.
I can share with an agreed audience.
I can record a response and a real next step.
words: The person or people you choose to share with.
A specific response that can help your next choice.
The actual item or record you are explaining.
Your thoughts about what you did and what comes next.

artist_cards.description: A helper looks at an empty shelf. The helper pauses with open hands. A friend points to a box. They both look in the box. They smile when the prop is found.
artist_cards.prompt: How does a still pose help us follow the story?
artist_cards.model_answer: The empty hands and look towards the shelf show a missing prop. The pause gives the viewer time to notice it.

artist_cards.description: Two makers hold an imaginary large sheet. They stop when it will not fit. One points to a fold. They fold the sheet in mime, then carry it together with space between them.
artist_cards.prompt: How does the second action show a new plan?
artist_cards.model_answer: They fold the sheet in mime so it fits. The action after the pause makes the change clear. Nobody needs a real prop or contact.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Choose your audience again.
Find Monday's selected item.
If it is missing, use today's fresh task.
stages.say: Check that you still agree with the audience plan. You may change to a private adult share. If a selected item is unavailable, we keep that gap honest and make a short real drama response today.
stages.good: Pupil reconfirms audience and has a genuine item or fresh route.
stages.fallback: Use the original fictional lost prop card for a short new contribution.
stages.answer: Audience choice can change. A new task is dated today and does not replace a missing past claim.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Listen to two viewer responses.
Which helps the maker?
You are good, or Your pause showed the change.
stages.say: The second response names a choice and its effect. We can use that information. A maker may disagree and explain why. We avoid judgements about the person.
stages.good: Pupil identifies specific feedback linked to a visible choice.
stages.fallback: Offer the two phrases orally with one repetition and thinking time.
stages.answer: Your pause showed the change is more useful because it explains what the viewer noticed. It is still the viewer's interpretation.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch a short evidence share.
This is the item. My part was ___.
I chose ___ because ___.
Ask one viewer question.
stages.say: I use an adult model plan. I explain: I directed the folded-sheet ending and added a pause to show a new plan. My viewer says the pause helped. I confirm that was my aim. If the viewer saw something else, I ask which detail led to that reading. My next step is to try a clearer facing.
stages.good: Adult models source, contribution, choice, reason, viewer response and next step.
stages.fallback: Read the model aloud. Pupil points to the item while adult uses the sentence frame.
stages.answer: The model shows a real share structure, not pupil evidence. Check: Which sentence tells us the maker's choice?

stages.name: We do
pupil: Rehearse your share with a partner or adult.
Name the item, your part and a choice.
Viewer says: I notice ___.
Maker confirms or explains.
stages.say: Take turns in the maker and viewer roles, or use an adult viewer. Ask permission before touching the work. If a pupil cannot explain the item yet, return to one choice and one reason. Do not write words they have not confirmed.
stages.good: Every pupil rehearses a short explanation or directs a rehearsal. Feedback stays specific and optional.
stages.fallback: Adult reads a pupil-confirmed phrase and asks a single choice question.
stages.answer: If the pupil can identify a choice, proceed to share. If not, make a fresh two-pose choice so there is a real contribution to explain. This is the hinge decision.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Prepare a short share with your chosen viewer.
Use a real item, or make a fresh tiny drama.
Explain one choice and its reason.
Listen to one response.
Log what you will keep or change.
stages.say: Use two or three minutes to prepare, then share in a pair, small group or privately. A fresh route is a two-pose lost prop drama, acted seated or directed. Try two endings and choose one. The viewer gives a specific response. Keep the pupil's own decision about using it. Do not demand a public performance or recording.
stages.good: Each pupil shares actual arts evidence or a new witnessed contribution, receives an audience response and records a reasoned next step.
stages.fallback: Pupil directs the adult performance and selects an ending by gesture. Adult states the confirmed choice to the agreed viewer. Pupil confirms the feedback record.
stages.answer: Example only: My viewer saw that the prop was found. I will keep the final pose but pause longer. If sharing is declined, record preparation and plan another opportunity honestly.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Name a choice you want to keep.
Name a small change, if one would help.
Check your viewer note is true.
Put the item back in your log.
stages.say: Read the note back to the maker. The maker can correct it. Separate what was shown from what is planned. In the last two minutes, store the item safely and clear the performance space.
stages.good: The maker confirms an accurate record, including disagreement or an uncompleted share where applicable.
stages.fallback: Read one short sentence and offer keep / change.
stages.answer: A true note might say shared privately with an adult, or prepared but not yet shared. Neither should be changed into a public performance claim.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: I shared ___ with ___.
They noticed ___.
I will ___ because ___.
stages.say: Record the audience type, your actual contribution, feedback and next step. Use no personal names in this template. Keep missing evidence marked as a gap. This is progress towards the award, not a completion claim.
stages.good: A dated sharing record preserves pupil voice and distinguishes completed evidence from future plans.
stages.fallback: Adult scribes a short oral or gestured response and reads it back.
stages.answer: Example only: I shared my two-pose drama with one adult. They noticed the ending. I will keep the pause because it helped the story.

Supported: Choose one real item or a fresh two-pose task.
Use the frame My part was ___.
Confirm one note and a next step.
Independent: Select genuine evidence and prepare a short explanation.
State your contribution, choice and reason.
Log what you will keep or change and why.
Aspire: Ask a precise question about your artistic choice.
Compare your aim with the viewer response.
Justify a next step and plan a way to check it.

log: I agree / see it differently because ___.
My next step is ___ and I will check it by ___.
misconceptions: Sharing must be a public performance
An agreed private adult audience is valid. Record the audience honestly.
Feedback must change the maker's work
The maker can keep a choice or change it for a reason.
A viewer can decide the maker's intention
Ask the maker to confirm or explain. Distinguish intention from audience interpretation.
A prepared share can be recorded as completed
Only record sharing that happened. Keep a declined or unfinished share as a future opportunity.
kit: For up to five pupils: available arts logs, books and pencils.
Access only each pupil's permitted records. Cover identifying details when sharing.
Adult model audit page clearly labelled Teacher model only.
No recording device, costume, prop or internet is required.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show the adult model plan and name the contribution.
15 to 30 seconds
Explain the pause and give a reason.
30 to 45 seconds
Read an invented viewer response clearly labelled Teacher model only.
45 to 60 seconds
Confirm the response and state a specific next step.
models: Teacher model only: I shared a plan of the folded-sheet story. I chose a pause to show the new plan. The viewer noticed it. I will test turning the last pose towards the audience.

staff_guidance.plain_language: A pause, a request for help or a new plan can show resilience. Pupils do not need to act out real distress or tell a personal story.
staff_guidance.scope: Both pathways work at Explore. Retain actual participation, exploration, creation and sharing evidence for the award. These lessons do not certify completion. Optional next level work in GROW is additional.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: Model a tiny invented action slowly. A clear choice matters more than expert acting. A pupil may direct an adult, use a seated gesture or describe the action.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Agree an open-hand stop signal and a quiet return cue. Keep voices at talking level. Allow pass, private sharing and a calm pause. Do not use sudden noises, personal stories or forced eye contact.
staff_guidance.safety: Clear bags and chairs from the acting area. Mark personal space by agreement; no touch, lifting, chasing, falls, climbing, weapons or thrown objects. Mime props. A still pose may be seated and lasts only a comfortable few seconds.
prompt_ladder: Point to the place or instruction.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Compare your aim with what the viewer saw. Will you use one idea they gave you? Say why. Set one skill to try. Say how you will check it.
stretch.evidence: Keep your real item, your own reason and the viewer's words. Add your skill goal and a plan to check it.

stretch.good: Pupil uses specific evidence from the share and keeps ownership of the artistic choice.
stretch.fallback: Adult asks the same questions one at a time and records the pupil's confirmed words. A private share is enough.

lessons.cover: Use selected arts evidence if available. Model a short evidence explanation and specific feedback. Let each pupil choose a peer, small group or private adult audience. If needed, create a new two-pose drama and date its evidence today. Record actual sharing, pupil response and a feasible next step. The seven stages total 40 minutes.

scope: Explore for both pathways. Optional GROW next level stretch retains additional evidence without changing core success criteria.
timing: Arrival 0-3; Starter 3-6; I do 6-12; We do 12-18; Create 18-32; Review 32-37; Exit 37-40 minutes.
